text:
maria: Heads-up — the new per-token span histogram on /v1/stream is showing a 2.3x bump in 'server:serialize_chunk' p95 after yesterday's kernel swap. Anyone else?
lee: Yep, saw that on the perf dashboard. p50 stable but p95 spikes mostly for requests that emit >1k tokens. :eyes:
sam: I rolled the kernel selector to prefer mmha-v2 for fp16 on canary around 17:40 UTC. Also tightened batching heuristic to fixed batch=8 to reduce tail latency.
maria: Hmm could be the kernel's AVX path for long kv sequences. Perf-bot alerted too.
perf-bot: ALERT: route=/v1/stream per-route p95 exceeded threshold (2s) at 1799127000. See /dash/perf/streams/route-p95
nisha: I ran a short perf run on canary, attaching top stacks (summarized): 'serialize_chunk' -> 48% memcpy, 30% flatten, 12% kernel_copy. Flamegraph suggests serialization overhead grows with chunk count.
lee: That matches client/server timing: client-chunk-sent -> server-start -> server:compute token -> server:serialize_chunk -> network. The extra memcpy hints at batching causing more fragmented chunks.
sam: Quick reproduce command:
```
./perf/run_stream_load.sh --model redwood-openv1 --seq 2048 --clients 4 --batching dynamic
```
Try dynamic batching or increase max_batch_size to 16.
maria: Can we add a token-level tag to spans so dashboards can split 'serialize' vs 'compute' per route? Need to see per-chunk serialization cost histograms.
nisha: I can push a lightweight instrumentation: add span.tag("chunk_phase", "serialize|compute|io") and emit token_index dimension. Low-risk.
lee: +1. Also add an A/B metric to compare mmha-v2 vs mmha-v1 for same payloads.
sam: I'll revert fixed batch=8 on canary for the next hour and enable nisha's span tags on a small subset.
maria: Plan: 1) revert batching; 2) add span tags; 3) rerun perf harness and link flamegraphs to dashboard. If p95 remains, consider kernel fallback. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: NOTE: runbook updated -> see ops/playbooks/streaming-serialization.md
maria: Thanks team — keep updates here.
